label: GO after a1 led rarely to S2 and was rewarded
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never at D1/D2), when the previous trial was a1 with a rare transition to S2 and was rewarded (a1 -> S2R, r1 at D1). All variables are observed by GO. Dev P=0.78 R=0.85 F1=0.82 mass recall 0.90. It essentially never fires after the mirror case (a2 -> S1 rare rewarded) or after common / unrewarded trials. Magnitude is modulated by the agent upcoming choice: when the agent stays with a1 (model-free-like repeat) it fires reliably and strongly (adding action==1 gives precision 0.96); when the agent switches to a2 (model-based response) it fires only ~56% of the time and weakly (27% of active steps but 15% of mass). Most misses are GO steps on the first window trial (rel -3) where the previous trial is outside the window, plus weak activations on other GO steps.

issues: Every factual claim held up when scored on dev. The feature fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps). Mirror case (GO, prev_action==2, rare, rewarded): recall 0. Common-rewarded a1 case: recall 0. Dropping prev_reward==1 or rel>-3 leaves recall unchanged and only lowers precision. Adding action==1 gives P 0.96, R 0.58, F1 0.72. Adding action==2 gives P 0.56, recall 0.27, mass 0.15. All of these match the explanation.
Test split reproduces the reported scores: P 0.766, R 0.853, F1 0.807, mass recall 0.898.

Misses (about 10% of activation mass on dev and test) are mostly GO at rel -3, where prev_action/prev_common is -1 (outside the window). That is a limit of the data, not a gap in the feature. The rest are scattered weak activations (<0.3).

The false positives are systematic, not noise. They are almost all predicate-true GO steps where the agent then switches to a2 (often at rel +1). The explanation already discloses this. They are explained by the agent's own policy logit: adding choice > -5 (the feature is silent when the agent strongly prefers a2) raises test precision to 0.88 with little recall loss, test F1 0.856 vs 0.807. This refines the predicate; it does not refute the label.
The label does not overclaim, and the predicate uses no future variables (choice is the agent's own computed logit, also legitimate).
